headline: Structure-aware models guide biomolecular sequence design and interaction prediction
label: Structure Informed Sequence Design
summary: Recent preprints extend structure-conditioned modeling from protein and regulatory sequences to multimodal RNA and protein foundation models.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit structural representation inside models that operate on biomolecular sequence. PISCO couples protein sequence, 3D structure, and host codon usage in a GVP-based network for species-specific codon optimization, and it generalizes to unseen settings. MIMIC extends this direction to a generative multimodal foundation model trained on the aligned LORE dataset, spanning sequence, structure, regulation, and evolution. What is new is the breadth of modalities entering a single representation rather than structure alone. CORAL and PROTEUS are adjacent rather than generative design: CORAL predicts RNA-protein interactions with bidirectional cross-attention over ESM-2 and DNABERT2 embeddings and stricter non-redundant benchmarks, while PROTEUS derives a zero-shot conformational plasticity score from SimpleFold flow-matching embeddings. The geometric pathogenicity framework addresses mutation effects rather than sequence design.
